title: In vivo dendritic cell reprogramming for cancer immunotherapy
source: Science TLDR podcast episode 7 show notes
one_line: Forced expression of the transcription factors PU.1, IRF8 and BATF3 (PIB) reprograms tumor cells in vivo into type 1 conventional dendritic-like cells, converting the tumor itself into an antigen-presenting vaccine.
key_claims: PIB overexpression reprograms tumor cells into cDC1-like cells in vivo and induces systemic antitumor immunity in mouse melanoma models.

Reprogrammed tumors remodel the microenvironment, recruiting and expanding polyclonal cytotoxic T cells and forming tertiary lymphoid structure-like aggregates, with CD4+ T cells acting as critical effectors.
Mice cleared by in vivo reprogramming are protected on tumor re-challenge, indicating long-term systemic immunological memory.
Reprogramming to immunogenic dendritic-like cells also occurs in human tumor spheroids and xenografts, independent of immunosuppression.
Adenoviral delivery of PIB in situ elicits potent antitumor responses even at low doses, and combined with immune checkpoint blockade produces complete tumor regression with durable memory.
limitations: The relative contribution of partially versus fully reprogrammed cells to the antitumor response was not resolved.
Long-term safety and efficacy in humans were not addressed; efficacy data are from mouse models and human spheroid/xenograft systems.
Delivery method and reprogramming efficiency still require optimization for clinical application.
No specific efficiency, dose or survival numbers are reported in the available material.
open_questions: Does adenoviral PIB delivery reprogram tumors and drive T cell responses in patients, in a first-in-human trial?
Would selective depletion or lineage tracing of fully versus partially reprogrammed cells show which population drives tumor rejection?
Is TLS formation in reprogrammed tumors a validated predictive biomarker of response?
Does combining in vivo cDC1 reprogramming with adoptive T cell therapy or agonistic CD40 antibodies add benefit over ICB combination?
